1.title: The Same Variety as German Riesling
1.html:
Riesling in Alsace is documented from the 15th century (earliest around 1477). It is the same variety as Riesling in the German Rhine regions; the stylistic differences come from soil, climate and winemaking: Alsace Riesling is mostly made dry, with higher alcohol.

Riesling is the most representative variety on the Alsace Rhine side and is widely regarded as the noblest and most refined variety in the whole of Alsace — it now covers 21.68% of the region's vineyard area, the most widely planted variety.
2.title: Late Ripening with a Distinctive Pattern
2.html:
• Ripening: a late-ripening variety (2e époque tardive) with unstable yields (46–78 hl/ha) and a natural alcohol of about 10.7°–12.1° under normal conditions
  • Distinctive trait: even at relatively low temperatures Riesling keeps ripening — which makes it especially suited to Alsace's cool conditions
  • Bunch and berry: small, cylindrical-conical, compact bunches; small round berries, pale green to golden, with delicate and fragrant flavours
3.title: Wine Style and Food Pairing
3.html:
Style: dry, lively acidity, clear and noble character — Alsatians call it "roi des vins d'Alsace" (king of Alsace wines). Fine Riesling seeks harmony between acidity and fruit and shows more or less mineral character depending on origin; top Riesling has outstanding ageing potential.

Food pairing: pan-fried or sauced fish (fish stew from the Ill, trout, pike-perch in butter sauce, skate wing in Nantais butter), shellfish, oysters, scallops, seafood platters, smoked salmon, and the classic Alsatian choucroute (sauerkraut).
4.question: What distinctive ripening trait of Alsace Riesling makes it especially suited to a cool region?
4.options.0: It needs extreme heat to ripen, so it can only be planted on sunny slopes
4.options.1: It keeps ripening even at relatively low temperatures
4.options.2: It is the earliest-ripening of all varieties and escapes autumn cold
4.options.3: It is unaffected by temperature and ripens in any conditions
4.explanation: Alsace Riesling is a late-ripening variety with a distinctive trait: it keeps ripening even at relatively low temperatures. This suits Alsace's cool semi-continental climate and is an important reason why it covers 21.68% of the vineyard area and is called "the king of Alsace wines".
